Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: key inputs and next steps

Hi Jordan — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size Dedicated for FinVault: 

1) Deployment mode: you said Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) is preferred due to predictable throughput and data isolation; noted that Private VPC is on the table later.
2) Immediate asks for sizing: could you confirm peak TPS targets, sustained TPS, expected concurrency, and a rough token mix (short/medium/long requests)? Also let us know whether you have a GPU preference (A100 vs H100) or if you want Redwood to recommend.
3) Perf constraints: are there strict latency SLOs (p50/p95) per request or any hard cutoff for tail latency?
4) Timeline & next steps: if you can share the sizing inputs (tokens per request distribution, % of requests that use system prompts, average context length), I'll run a quick capacity calc and share a recommended starting config + cost estimate. We can then schedule a technical kickoff with Marissa to validate infra details.

I attached a simple Excel you can fill (FinVault_Dedicated_Sizing_Inputs.xlsx) — feel free to drop values inline if easier.

Thanks —

Thanks Aditya — filling this out inline to keep things moving. I've also attached the completed sizing sheet.

High level usage:
- Peak TPS: 40 requests/sec (brief spikes around batch runs)
- Sustained TPS: ~12 requests/sec average over business hours
- Typical concurrency: 4-6 concurrent long-running sessions (supporting active users); up to 10 concurrent short queries during peak

Token mix (approx):
- 60% short queries (100-200 tokens total)
- 30% medium (400-800 tokens total)
- 10% long (1,500-2,500 tokens, multi-turn summaries)

Average token breakdown:~ input 350 tokens / output 450 tokens for medium requests; long jobs have ~3k total tokens processed (including context).

Latency targets:
- p50 < 150ms for short queries
- p95 < 750ms for medium queries
- long jobs can be slower (we're OK with seconds-scale for large summaries)

GPU preference: we prefer H100s if pricing delta is reasonable; if Redwood recommends A100 for cost efficiency that's fine too.

Timeline: we are aiming for a pilot environment in early December for a 2-week evaluation. Procurement is looped to start on PO terms.

Jordan Lee
Head of ML Platform, FinVault
jordan.lee@finvault.com

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: recommendation + trial proposal

Appreciate the details, Jordan — this is great. Based on the numbers you provided, here's an initial recommendation and proposed next steps: 

Recommendation (baseline):
- GPU type: H100 (preferred given long-job throughput and mixed token profile). We'll provide an alternate A100-based config if you want a lower-cost option.
- Initial reserved capacity: 2x H100 nodes (each node sized to serve ~20 peak TPS with target batching/kv-cache enabled).
- Autoscale/burst: allow burst to 4x H100s to cover short peak windows (handles your 40 TPS spikes and concurrency up to ~10).
- Concurrency config: tune max concurrent request slots to 12 with queueing & soft timeouts for long jobs.

Rationale: with ~60% short queries and 30% medium, continuous batching + prefix caching will reduce per-token cost and keep short-query p50/p95 targets achievable. Long jobs will be scheduled onto free capacity and can span longer runtimes.

Pilot & next steps:
1) Start a 2-week pilot on Dedicated (2x H100 baseline, autoscale to 4) in early Dec. Redwood provides monitoring + per-route latency/cost dashboards during the trial.
2) Redwood will share a preliminary pricing estimate and SLA PDF — attached (SLA-Dedicated.pdf).
3) Technical kickoff — Marissa, can you own the technical kickoff and invite infra/DevOps from FinVault? Suggested dates: Dec 1-3.
4) Procurement: Jordan, if procurement can start the PO process we'll prepare a temporary trial agreement and the procurement packet.

I attached the SLA and the capacity inputs (filled). If that looks good I'll run a more detailed cost calc and send a formal pilot proposal + DocuSign link for the trial agreement.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
